memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "As for you, be fruitful and increase in number; multiply on the earth and increase upon it." - Gen 9:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God repeats the call He gave at the start of the chapter: "be fruitful and increase in number." This gentle repetition is not accidental. God is emphasising His purpose for Noah and his family - to fill the emptied earth with life once more. After the devastation of the flood, God's heart is set on flourishing, on life springing up and spreading across the world again.

There is something deeply encouraging in this. God is not a God of destruction but of life. The flood was judgement, but God's lasting purpose is blessing and fruitfulness. He looks at an emptied world and says, "Let it be full of life again." He is always working toward renewal, restoration, and flourishing.

This tells us about God's character and His hopes for us. He wants our lives to be fruitful - not barren, not stuck, not defined forever by the losses behind us. Whatever floods have swept through your life, God's purpose for you is fruitfulness on the other side.

Jesus took up this same theme when He said, "I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full" (John 10:10). The God who called Noah to fill the earth calls us to bear fruit that lasts (John 15:16). His purpose for His people has always been life and fruitfulness. Step into the new season God gives you, trusting that He is a God who brings flourishing out of what once seemed empty.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God's purpose for you is fruitfulness, not barrenness?
- What might it look like to step into a fruitful new season with God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: God of life, thank You that Your purpose is always flourishing, not destruction. Bring fruitfulness out of the empty places in my life, and help me bear fruit that lasts, for Your glory.
